key_themes: Intel/Apple chip deal drives semiconductor and memory surge
Iran peace deal collapses oil prices, pressures energy sector
Fed holds rates but signals 2026 rate hike — markets recover from June 17 selloff
AI infrastructure demand (SNDK, MU, CRWV) lifts Nasdaq to +1.91%
Earnings season: ACN and KR disappoint on guidance despite revenue beats
notes: June 19 is Juneteenth (market holiday). Data reflects June 18 close. S&P 500 and Nasdaq values are estimates based on percentage changes reported; Dow Jones closed at ~51,564 (+0.14%), Russell 2000 at 2,979.77 (+2.12%).

stocks.reason: Trump announced Apple-Intel chip manufacturing partnership — Intel to design and build chips for Apple in the US. Stock surged 8.5–9.5% on June 18.
Jumped 10.48% on June 18 after Apple flagged unavoidable memory price hikes; AI/NAND flash shortage narrative reinforced; beneficiary of Intel/Apple deal.
Q3 FY2026 earnings: revenue of $18.7B missed consensus; guided Q4 below expectations; lowered full-year revenue growth to 3–4%; new bookings fell YoY. Stock dropped ~14–18% on June 18.

Q1 FY2026 earnings on June 18: revenue beat ($46.1B vs $45.35B est.) but profitability concerns; same-store sales +1.0% vs prior +3.2%; EPS guidance midpoint of $5.20 below $5.24 consensus. Stock dropped ~8%.
Barclays upgrade on June 18 and production shipments of IQ9S microinverters began; stock up 4–10% on the session.
Trump signed Iran peace deal on June 18, reopening Strait of Hormuz; crude oil fell toward $80/barrel from ~$120 highs, dragging Exxon and broader energy sector down 2%+.
FDA approved Utebzi (tebipenem pivoxil) on June 17 — first oral carbapenem antibiotic for complicated UTIs in the US, developed with GSK. Stock rose ~16% on June 18.
Gained 4%+ in premarket June 18, riding the Intel/Apple chip deal tailwinds and broader memory/NAND shortage narrative boosted by SNDK surge.

Added $32B to AI infrastructure backlog; upcoming Nasdaq-100 inclusion on June 22 driving passive fund demand; multiple new analyst initiations including Cantor Fitzgerald (Buy, $167 target). Stock up ~19% on the week.
Q1 2026 bookings surged ~2,000% YoY to $33.4M including a $20M system sale; Mizuho raised price target to $35; stock up 8.3% on June 18.
Wolfe Research downgraded to Peer Perform from Outperform on June 19, citing "elevated expectations," valuation that "looks full," and modest room for upside after a two-year re-rating.

Continued trading attention after June 12 IPO (closed at $160.95, +19% vs $135 IPO price); largest IPO in stock market history at ~$2.1T market cap; active discussion ahead of first full week of trading.
Cruise and travel stocks rallied June 18 as Iran peace deal and end of Middle East blockade signal improved global travel outlook; analyst raised price target on Carnival.
